title: I built Slime Trader with AI - even the servers and marketplace trading system
author: Fun_Examination8599
selftext:
I’m the developer behind **Slime Trader**.

I thought this community might find it interesting, so I wanted to share my game here.

Every part of Slime Trader was made using AI, except for the slime artwork. That includes the game code, UI, servers for the online features, marketplace trading system, and even the background music.

**I even made the trailer using Codex!**

Trailer:  
[https://youtu.be/PV45p\_kShYg?si=FccEsc3j8h7kS9yZ](https://youtu.be/PV45p_kShYg?si=FccEsc3j8h7kS9yZ)

The game is all about summoning and merging cute slimes to wipe out waves of bugs. You work toward higher-tier slimes, discover their different attack patterns, and adjust your formation as your collection grows stronger.

I also added leaderboards, marketplace trading, minigames to play with friends, and chat. Rather than making a game where you just watch numbers go up on your own, I wanted it to feel like a world you share with other players.

**The game hit 1,000 concurrent players on launch day!**  
(That dropped as low as 60 after the servers crashed, but we’re back in the 800s now—looks like we might hit a new all-time peak today!!)

Just a heads-up: the servers crashed quite a bit early on, so the reviews aren’t great, haha. I used AI for all the server fixes too, and things seem to be running smoothly now.

How far have you taken AI in your own game development? I’d love to hear from anyone who has used it not just for code or artwork, but also for server development, music production, or even trailers. Honest feedback on the game is welcome too!

Steam:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5164660/Slime\_Trader/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5164660/Slime_Trader/)

**Thank you!**
